episode_summary: Episode 257 (May 2019): the hosts and a roundtable including Jordan Spence of MyCrypto discuss the May 2019 Bitcoin and Ethereum price moves, Lightning Network usage and capacity, SegWit adoption, crypto UX, a Binance account-compromise hack, crypto insurance, and Devcon5 in Osaka.

cards.claim: On 11 May 2019 Bitcoin had been at $7,200 before retracing.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It was at $7,200, but it retraced back.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Ethereum had touched $200 and was trading at about $192.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Ethereum touched over 200. It's now at 192.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host predicted Bitcoin would reach $8,000 by August.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It's going to 8 by August.

cards.claim: In spring 2019 a host predicted Bitcoin would reach $6,000 within two weeks, but it took about a week longer.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: i said three weeks ago we'll be at 6 000 in two weeks and i was wrong

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host said there were more fiat on-ramps to Ethereum than ever before.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: there's more on-ramps from fiat to Ethereum than there's ever been.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host said Bitcoin had recently processed more transactions than ever, with fees about 68% below 2017 levels.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: People need to understand that Bitcoin did more transactions than it's ever done a few weeks

cards.claim: In May 2019 SegWit adoption was reported at about 42.59%, down from a peak of around 50%.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: SegWit adoption looked like it just peaked at 50%, and now it's currently at 42.59%.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host argued that no one would make money from the Lightning Network.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: The problem is no one's going to make money from lightning.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Lightning Network capacity was about $7.5 million.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: There's 7.5 million dollars in the capacity right now.

cards.claim: In May 2019 the Lightning Network had about 38,000 channels and 8,337 nodes.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: 38,000 channels. 8,337 nodes.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host argued the Lightning Network was designed for very low-value, high-volume payments.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: The Lightning Network was designed for very low value transactions at high volume.

cards.claim: In May 2019 hosts said Neutrino let users run a Lightning node on a phone without downloading the full Bitcoin blockchain.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: What about the advancement that Neutrino did, where you can launch a Lightning Note on your phone now because you don't need to look at the entire Bitcoin blockchain?

cards.claim: In May 2019 the Ethereum Foundation announced plans to spend $30 million on ecosystem development over the next 12 months.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: The Ethereum Foundation plans to spend $30 million on ecosystem development over the next 12 months.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host argued people had been convinced Bitcoin's only value was as a store of value, which kept it from being spent.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It's because people have been convinced that the only value that Bitcoin has is storage of value.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host argued the ecosystem had to make it acceptable to spend bitcoin before adoption could grow.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: But if you want to convince the whole entire ecosystem, you must make it acceptable to spend Satoshi.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host predicted Lightning Network usage would grow over time despite very little real use.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I think it's just a matter of time.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host argued crypto developers were not designing for the average person.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: These guys that are developing a system, they're not thinking of the average person.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host argued many crypto companies were built by engineers without designers, which made their products hard to use.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: a lot of the companies aren't hiring designers. They're built by engineers.

cards.claim: In May 2019 the hosts discussed a roughly 7,000-unit Binance hack that Binance attributed to user accounts compromised over time.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: They said it was users accounts that were like compromised over time.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host advised individual users not to give exchange API keys withdrawal permissions, only read-only or trade access.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Really, if you're an individual user, unless you really, really, really know what you're doing, you should not be giving anything withdrawal permissions.

cards.claim: In May 2019 a guest said he was building crypto insurance that would be priced by the market rather than backed by an exchange.
cards.speaker: guest
cards.quote: i'm working on blockchain or crypto insurance

cards.claim: In May 2019 the hosts explained insurance as risk transfer, with many small premiums pooled to cover rare large losses.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: everyone's just contributing a little bit and it's it's risk transfer

cards.claim: In May 2019 Devcon5 was scheduled for October 8 to 11, 2019.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It's in October. October 8th through the 11th, so it won't be on Halloween

cards.claim: In May 2019 Devcon5 was announced for Osaka, Japan.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It's in Osaka, Japan.

cards.claim: In May 2019 the hosts debated Consensus versus Devcon, with one saying Consensus was for suits and Devcon for developers.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: consensus consensus is for suits DEFCON is for developers

cards.claim: In May 2019 a proposed chain reorg to reverse the Binance theft was dismissed by Bitcoin experts as crazy talk.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: everybody who knows Bitcoin was like you are talking crazy talk

cards.claim: In May 2019 a host said he would be surprised if Bitcoin did not eventually climb above $90,000.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I think I'll be surprised if we don't go higher than 90,000.

title: The Bitcoin Podcast #257
